correctness.rationale: The first-node Lanczos Ritz value is exactly the Gaussian Rayleigh quotient. Gaussian radius/angular independence yields the displayed bias; Jensen establishes nonnegativity and strict coordinatewise log-eigenvalue convexity forces every maximizer onto a spectral box vertex. Dirichlet aggregation yields the beta integral. The closed dimension-two evaluation, beta-moment Taylor expansion, and dominated-convergence high-conditioning expansion derive the remaining exact conclusions. Replayed Python 3 standard-library tests returned VERIFY_OK 3934; tests are ancillary, not a proof of the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The one-node Gaussian Lanczos logdet estimator is a natural minimum-cost Krylov surrogate. Its systematic overestimate affects practical calibration and cannot be read off from ordinary trace unbiasedness. This theorem solves a condition-number-constrained expected-error extremal problem in every dimension, attains it with explicit two-level spectra, and proves a nontrivial near- versus far-conditioning optimizing-multiplicity change. It is stronger than a sign/Jensen check and supplies exact quantitative benchmarks without claiming multistep performance.
